mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-38.7 to -31.9). This momentum reflects underlying reopening inertia that persists absent a shock, continuing to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each week from -38.7 to -31.9 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its last-28-day mean in the subsequent 28 days despite three prior weeks of continuous improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility signals newly imposed or tightened restrictions on in-person work, which typically precedes reduced discretionary retail trips as overall activity contracts, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-over-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -23.9 (t-1w) to -29.0 (t-0w), a 5.1 point decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite a WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeding 4 points.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -39.1 to -21.7 while TRANSIT stayed in a narrow -40 to -44 band
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks even when PARKS rises more than 5 points WoW with TRANSIT stable.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the following week despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 13% throughout.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks despite a GROCERY_PHARM uptick exceeding 3 points with flat RETAIL_REC.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks despite PARKS maintaining or extending its upward trend.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained between -40.3 and -44.3 while WORKPLACES fluctuated narrowly around -24 to -29
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks even though TRANSIT stays below -38 and WORKPLACES rises more than 2 points WoW.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed within a 1.4-point range (12.7-14.1) across all four weeks
